newsitem.title: GERMANY: Witnesses saw youths at scene of fatal German fire.
newsitem.headline: Witnesses saw youths at scene of fatal German fire.

text.p: Three eyewitnesses giving evidence at the trial of a Lebanese man charged with starting a fire that killed 10 people said on Wednesday they saw three young men near the scene in an east German car.

The witnesses told the court that they saw the three standing beside a Wartburg car in the early morning hours of January 18, shortly after a deadly fire broke out at the refugee centre in this northern German town.
Their testimony cast doubt on prosecution arguments that the fire that killed 10 and injured 38 was started by a Lebanese man, Safwan Eid, who lived in the house.

Eid is on trial charged with aggravated arson and causing bodily harm. Prosecutors say Eid, a civil war refugee who lived in the hostel with his family for six years, was trying to get revenge in a petty quarrel with another resident.

The January fire in Luebeck, near the former border with East Germany, was the worst ever disaster to hit a foreigners' hostel. It initially raised fears of a new wave of neo-Nazi racist violence similar to one which swept the country after unification in 1990.
In court on Wednesday, two workers at a flour mill near the refugee centre testified that they saw three young men standing beside the Wartburg car at the time of the fire.
They said one of the young men had worn a long pony tail and another was wearing olive green pants, similar to the clothing worn by the German army.
A third witness, a postal worker on his way to work, also testified on Wednesday that he saw three young men near the scene of the fire, looking up at the house.
Eid's defence attorney said that the testimony supported their arguments that investigators had failed to conduct a thorough investigation.

Four youths from the eastern town of Grevensmuehle were initially detained by police shortly after the fire after a police squad car spotted the car in the vicinity of the fire. But the four were later released.
The fire killed six people from Zaire, a man from Benin, a Lebanese and a woman from Angola and her six-year-old daughter.
